idiom_name: Sequel DB[:users] dataset (insert/where/update/delete, rows as hashes)
implementation_notes: Sequel gives the gateway as a dataset: DB[:users] is a frozen, lazily evaluated per-table accessor whose insert/update/delete/where/order methods build SQL and whose iteration yields symbol-keyed hashes - the records - so a table's SQL lives in one dataset plus a thin module of named query methods (dataset.prepare for repeated statements). It is the toolbox form of Active Record: rows become objects only if you opt into Sequel::Model. ActiveRecord's own table-level query interface works the same way, but it pulls the row-object mapping along and is properly a different pattern.
code_sketch:
USERS = DB[:users]                            # one dataset per table

def find_user(id) = USERS.where(id: id).first   # -> symbol-keyed hash
def insert_user(row) = USERS.insert(row)        # returns the new primary key
def rename(id, name) = USERS.where(id: id).update(name: name)
pitfalls: Datasets are lazy: without a terminal call (.all, .first, .each) the statement never executes, and a gateway method that forgets one looks like a no-op.
Record hashes are symbol-keyed per selected column; joins, aliases and select changes rename keys, so callers that assume a fixed shape break silently.
Sequel::Model on the same table reintroduces a second mapping path (Active Record) beside the dataset - pick one per table.
Identifiers are quoted by the library, but raw SQL fragments passed as strings are not - interpolating caller input there is injection.
